key_insight: A low-pressure xenon plasma cell can convert deep-UV laser light into electricity with very high predicted efficiency by using photoionization plus magnetically guided charge separation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new receiver architecture for space laser power beaming that may avoid the thermal and recombination losses that limit semiconductor photovoltaic receivers.
method: Particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulation of a xenon-filled chamber under 58.4 nm pulsed laser illumination
Magnetic bias and chamber electric fields used to separate photoelectrons from ions
Parameter sweeps over bias voltage, magnetic field, and gas pressure to identify controlling design factors
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a steady-state laser-to-electrical conversion efficiency of 82.25% at 2000 W/m2 average incident power, with energy accounting closing to 1% in simulation.
watch_item: The concept is still simulation-based and depends on deep-UV laser operation plus precise plasma confinement conditions, which may be challenging to realize in a practical space receiver.
paper_title: Laser power transmission in space: Plasma-based power cell
